meta.generated_by: IBM Bob AI Code Review Coach

nodes.label: ibm-bob-review-coach
nodes.details: Sample Flask/Python application reviewed by IBM Bob AI Code Review Coach. 55 total findings across 4 dimensions.
nodes.fix: Work through findings by priority: Critical first, then High, Medium, Low.

nodes.label:
Security
16 findings
nodes.details: 16 security vulnerabilities found: 3 Critical, 7 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low. Scanned by IBM Bob security subagent.
nodes.fix: Start with SEC-001 (pickle.loads) and SEC-002 (command injection) — both are Critical RCE risks.

nodes.label:
Code Quality
15 findings
nodes.details: 15 code quality issues: 4 High, 7 Medium, 4 Low. Includes duplicated logic, high complexity, and missing error handling.
nodes.fix: Merge duplicated functions (QUA-001, QUA-002) first — they have the highest maintenance cost.

nodes.label:
Test Coverage
23 untested functions
nodes.details: 23 public functions had zero test coverage. IBM Bob test subagent generated 31 pytest tests (all pass). Flask routes still need integration tests.
nodes.fix: 31 unit tests generated in sample_app/tests/test_services.py. Add Flask route integration tests next.

nodes.label:
Documentation
24 missing docstrings
nodes.details: 24 of 24 public functions were missing docstrings. IBM Bob docs subagent generated Google-style docstrings in *_documented.py files.
nodes.fix: Apply docstrings from *_documented.py files back to the originals and remove the companion files.

nodes.label:
SEC-001
Unsafe Deserialization
nodes.details: pickle.loads(data_bytes) deserializes arbitrary bytes with no validation. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload that executes arbitrary OS commands during deserialization.
nodes.fix: Replace pickle entirely. Use json for user preferences. If binary serialization is unavoidable, use HMAC-signed payloads and validate the schema before loading.

nodes.label:
SEC-002
Command Injection
nodes.details: subprocess.call("python reports/" + report_name, shell=True) passes user input directly to a shell. Injecting ; or && executes arbitrary host commands.
nodes.fix: Use subprocess.run(["python", f"reports/{report_name}"], shell=False) and whitelist valid report filenames before use.

nodes.label:
SEC-003
Info Disclosure /debug
nodes.details: The unauthenticated /debug GET endpoint returns the database password, API key, and JWT secret in plaintext JSON to any network-accessible client.
nodes.fix: Remove the /debug endpoint entirely. Health checks should return only {"status": "ok"} behind authentication.

nodes.label:
SEC-004
SQL Injection (get_user)
nodes.details: Username is concatenated directly into a SQL string. Classic ' OR '1'='1 bypass is possible.
nodes.fix: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?", (username,))

nodes.label:
SEC-005
SQL Injection (create_user)
nodes.details: Python %-formatting builds the INSERT statement from user-supplied values, exploitable by injection through username or email.
nodes.fix: cursor.execute("INSERT INTO users (username, password, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (username, hashed, email))

nodes.label:
SEC-006
SQL Injection (update_email)
nodes.details: new_email is concatenated into the UPDATE string; user_id cast provides no SQL safety.
nodes.fix: cursor.execute("UPDATE users SET email = ? WHERE id = ?", (new_email, user_id))

nodes.label:
SEC-007
Hardcoded Secrets
nodes.details: DB_PASSWORD and API_KEY are committed in plaintext. Any repository reader obtains production credentials.
nodes.fix: Load from environment variables: os.environ["DB_PASSWORD"], os.environ["API_KEY"].

nodes.label:
SEC-008
Hardcoded JWT Secret
nodes.details: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded; a leaked key allows forging authentication tokens for any user.
nodes.fix: JWT_SECRET = os.environ["JWT_SECRET"] with a >=256-bit random value.

nodes.label:
SEC-009
Broken Auth (static token)
nodes.details: Every successful login returns "token": "static-token-123". This static string makes session management illusory.
nodes.fix: Issue a properly signed, time-limited JWT containing the authenticated user's identity.

nodes.label:
SEC-010
Password Hash Exposed
nodes.details: The /user/<username> endpoint requires no authentication and returns password_hash in the response body.
nodes.fix: Require a valid session. Never include credential fields in API responses.

nodes.label:
SEC-011
Weak Crypto (MD5)
nodes.details: Unsalted MD5 is used for password hashing. MD5 is cryptographically broken and trivially reversible with rainbow tables.
nodes.fix: Replace with bcrypt, argon2-cffi, or hashlib.scrypt with a per-user random salt.

nodes.label:
SEC-012
No Order Ownership Check
nodes.details: Any caller can cancel any order by supplying an arbitrary order_id. No ownership or role check.
nodes.fix: Verify the authenticated user owns the order. Return HTTP 403 if not.

nodes.label:
SEC-013
Unauth Order Placement
nodes.details: The /order POST endpoint has no authentication guard — unauthenticated clients can place orders.
nodes.fix: Add @login_required or equivalent middleware to the route.

nodes.label:
SEC-014
Flask debug=True
nodes.details: app.run(debug=True, host="0.0.0.0") exposes Werkzeug interactive debugger with a remote Python shell.
nodes.fix: Set debug=False. Serve with Gunicorn/uWSGI. Control via FLASK_DEBUG env var.

nodes.label:
SEC-015
No Input Validation (user)
nodes.details: No length or format checks on user creation fields. Oversized inputs may cause unexpected DB behavior.
nodes.fix: Enforce max-length constraints. Return HTTP 400 on violations.

nodes.label:
SEC-016
No Input Validation (order)
nodes.details: Negative or non-numeric qty/price produce invalid totals or unhandled exceptions.
nodes.fix: Validate positive numeric types before processing. Return HTTP 422 on invalid input.

nodes.label:
QUA-001
Duplicate Score Logic
nodes.details: calculate_admin_score is a verbatim copy of calculate_user_score. Any change must be applied twice — divergence is inevitable.
nodes.fix: Delete calculate_admin_score. Use calculate_user_score everywhere, or add a role parameter.

nodes.label:
QUA-002
Duplicate Order Logic
nodes.details: process_bulk_order duplicates the entire body of process_order. Only the status field differs.
nodes.fix: Extract _calculate_order(order_data, status) helper. Both public functions become one-liners.

nodes.label:
QUA-003
High Complexity
nodes.details: calculate_user_score has 4 levels of nesting and cyclomatic complexity ~8. Repeated if-bonus pattern in each tier.
nodes.fix: Use a lookup table [(threshold, rate, bonus_rate)] and apply bonus in a single post-step.

nodes.label:
QUA-004
SRP Violation (create_user)
nodes.details: create_user mixes password hashing, SQL construction, and DB I/O. Hashing step is untestable without a live DB.
nodes.fix: Extract hash_password(password) helper. Manage connections via context manager.

nodes.label:
QUA-005
SRP Violation (debug route)
nodes.details: /debug endpoint hard-codes the same credential strings from user_service.py, creating a second source-of-truth and unauthenticated secret exposure.
nodes.fix: Remove /debug entirely for production. If needed, gate behind app.debug and return only non-sensitive info.

nodes.label:
QUA-006
Magic Numbers (discounts)
nodes.details: Multipliers 0.90, 0.80, 0.50 appear inline with no named constant. Intent is unclear to future maintainers.
nodes.fix: DISCOUNT_RATES = {"SAVE10": 0.10, "SAVE20": 0.20, "HALFOFF": 0.50}. Apply as 1 - rate.

nodes.label:
QUA-007
Magic Numbers (thresholds)
nodes.details: Quantity thresholds 100, 50 and multipliers 0.9, 0.95 appear as bare literals in two duplicated code blocks.
nodes.fix: Define BULK_TIER_LARGE, BULK_TIER_MEDIUM, DISCOUNT_LARGE, DISCOUNT_MEDIUM constants.

nodes.label:
QUA-008
Dead Code (stub)
nodes.details: get_order_history contains only pass — silently returns None. Callers expecting a list get a silent TypeError.
nodes.fix: raise NotImplementedError("get_order_history is not yet implemented").

nodes.label:
QUA-009
Bare Dict Access (orders)
nodes.details: Both order functions access dict keys without guard. A missing key raises an unhandled KeyError.
nodes.fix: Use order_data.get(key) with explicit checks, or validate with pydantic/marshmallow at the API boundary.

nodes.label:
QUA-010
Bare Dict Access (API)
nodes.details: Incomplete JSON body raises unhandled KeyError in create_user_api with no HTTP 400 path.
nodes.fix: Use .get() with null checks. Return HTTP 400 on missing required fields.

nodes.label:
QUA-011
Inconsistent Naming
nodes.details: Some functions use username (string), others use user_id (int). No consistent primary-key convention.
nodes.fix: Resolve username→id at the API boundary. Use user_id consistently in internal service calls.

nodes.label:
QUA-012
DB Connection Leaks
nodes.details: conn.close() only runs on the happy path. Exceptions cause connection leaks throughout all DB functions.
nodes.fix: Use with contextlib.closing(get_db_connection()) as conn: throughout.

nodes.label:
QUA-013
Hardcoded Port
nodes.details: Port 5000 is a bare literal. Changing it requires a source edit.
nodes.fix: port = int(os.environ.get("PORT", 5000))

nodes.label:
QUA-014
Unused Import
nodes.details: import os is present but os is never referenced. Misleads readers into thinking env vars are used.
nodes.fix: Remove the import os line.

nodes.label:
QUA-015
Inconsistent Return Style
nodes.details: authenticate_user returns bool but get_user returns a raw DB row tuple. Callers rely on tuple truthiness inconsistently.
nodes.fix: Define a User dataclass. Return it or None from all user-fetching functions. Add type annotations.

nodes.label:
TST-001
31 Tests Generated
nodes.details: 23 public functions had zero test coverage before this review. IBM Bob test subagent generated 31 pytest tests (all pass) using mocked SQLite. Flask routes still lack integration tests.
nodes.fix: Run: cd sample_app && python -m pytest tests/ --cov=src. Add Flask route integration tests using app.test_client().

nodes.label:
DOC-001
24 Docstrings Generated
nodes.details: 24 of 24 public functions were missing docstrings. IBM Bob docs subagent generated Google-style docstrings in *_documented.py companion files.
nodes.fix: Apply docstrings from *_documented.py back to the originals and delete the companion files.
